To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechano-response of AF cells derived from degenerated IVDs differed from non-degenerated AF cells.
the mechano-responses of human AF cells derived from degenerated and non-degenerated IVDs are different.
integrin – dependent mechanotransduction is altered in mechanically stimulated AF cells derived with degeneration, suggesting an alternative mechano-response pathway operates with IVD disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the altered, and/or alternative, mechanotrasduction pathway operating with degeneration in human annulus fibroblasts.
the role of integrin – dependent mechanotransduction in human annulus fibrosis cells.
the mechanobiological response of human annulus cells to mechanical loading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanotransduction mechanisms operating in human AF cells derived from degenerated IVDs are not fully understood, but may be different from those in non-degenerate AF.
RGD -recognising integrins are involved in mechanotransduction in AF cells derived non-degenerate IVDs and this may be an important mechanotransduction mechanism in the non-degenerate AF.

integrin -dependent signalling pathways may play a role in the mechano-response in AF cells from non -degenerate tissue, but not degeneration, where a distinct mechanotransduction process may be operating.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

RGD -recognizing integrins and associated FAK signalling are involved in the CTS response of non-degenerate, human AF cells but that this pathway is altered or absent in degenerate AF cell populations.
integrin -dependent mechanotransduction is altered in degenerate IVD cells, and this is potentially linked to the altered mechano-response observed with degeneration.
integrins are involved in mechanotransduction in human annulus fibroblast cells derived from healthy tissue, however, with disc degeneration, an alternative mechanotansduction pathway operates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response of human AF cells to mechanical stimuli is altered with degeneration.
RGD-integrins may be involved in the 0.1 Hz CTS – dependent mechano-response observed, in AF cells derived, from non-degenerate IVDs, but not those derived from degenerate IVD tissue.
we have identified an alternative mechanotranduction pathway operating with degeneration in IVD cells.
